chapters.title: God creates the world
chapters.summary: In six days God speaks light, sky, land, sea, plants, lights in the sky and living creatures into being, and calls it good. Last He makes humankind in His own image to care for the earth.

chapters.title: The garden and the first couple
chapters.summary: God rests on the seventh day. A closer telling follows: the man formed from dust, the garden of Eden, the one forbidden tree, and the woman made as his partner.

chapters.title: The fall
chapters.summary: The serpent tempts the woman, and the man and woman eat the forbidden fruit. Shame and blame enter, curses follow, and they leave the garden, yet God clothes them and promises the serpent's defeat.

chapters.title: Cain and Abel
chapters.summary: Cain kills his brother Abel out of jealousy and is sent away, still under God's protection. Cain's line builds cities and crafts, while Seth is born and people begin to call on the Lord.

chapters.title: From Adam to Noah
chapters.summary: A family line runs ten generations from Adam to Noah. Each life ends with "and he died", except Enoch, who walked with God and was taken.

chapters.title: A world gone wrong
chapters.summary: Violence fills the earth and grieves God. He tells Noah, a righteous man, to build an ark for his family and the animals.

chapters.title: The flood
chapters.summary: Noah, his family and the animals enter the ark, and the waters cover the earth for many days. Every living thing outside the ark dies.

chapters.title: The waters go down
chapters.summary: God remembers Noah. The raven and the dove go out, the earth dries, and Noah builds an altar. God promises never again to destroy the earth this way.

chapters.title: The rainbow covenant
chapters.summary: God blesses Noah's family and makes a covenant with every living thing, sealed with the rainbow. Noah's drunkenness leads to a curse on Canaan, Ham's son.

chapters.title: The table of nations
chapters.summary: A list of Noah's descendants through Shem, Ham and Japheth shows how the peoples of the ancient world spread out across the lands.

chapters.title: The tower of Babel
chapters.summary: People build a city and tower to make a name for themselves. God confuses their language and scatters them. The line of Shem leads to Abram.

chapters.title: The call of Abram
chapters.summary: God calls Abram to leave his country for a land He will show him, promising to make him a great nation and a blessing to all families of the earth. In Egypt, Abram passes Sarai off as his sister.

chapters.title: Abram and Lot part
chapters.summary: Their flocks grow too large to live together, so Lot chooses the well-watered Jordan plain near Sodom. God renews His promise of land and countless descendants to Abram.

chapters.title: Abram rescues Lot
chapters.summary: Abram defeats four kings to rescue Lot. Melchizedek, king of Salem and priest of God Most High, blesses him, and Abram gives him a tenth.

chapters.title: God's covenant with Abram
chapters.summary: Abram believes God's promise that his descendants will be as many as the stars, and it is counted to him as righteousness. God seals a covenant in a night vision with a smoking pot and a flaming torch.

chapters.title: Hagar and Ishmael
chapters.summary: Sarai gives her servant Hagar to Abram, and tension follows. Hagar runs away, but the angel of the Lord finds her in the desert. She names Him "the God who sees me."

chapters.title: The sign of circumcision
chapters.summary: God renames Abram as Abraham and Sarai as Sarah, promises them a son, and gives circumcision as the sign of the covenant for Abraham's household.

chapters.title: Three visitors
chapters.summary: Abraham welcomes three visitors who promise that Sarah will have a son, and Sarah laughs. Abraham then pleads with God to spare Sodom for the sake of the righteous.

chapters.title: Sodom and Gomorrah
chapters.summary: Angels rescue Lot's family before fire destroys Sodom and Gomorrah. Lot's wife looks back and becomes a pillar of salt. The chapter ends with the troubling origins of Moab and Ammon.

chapters.title: Abraham and Abimelech
chapters.summary: Abraham again says Sarah is his sister, and King Abimelech takes her. God warns the king in a dream, and Sarah is returned unharmed.

chapters.title: Isaac is born
chapters.summary: God keeps His promise and Sarah gives birth to Isaac. Hagar and Ishmael are sent away, but God provides water and promises Ishmael a future.

chapters.title: The binding of Isaac
chapters.summary: God tests Abraham by asking him to offer Isaac on a mountain in Moriah. At the last moment the angel stops him and God provides a ram instead.

chapters.title: Sarah's burial
chapters.summary: Sarah dies at Hebron. Abraham buys the cave of Machpelah from the Hittites, his first piece of the promised land, to bury her.

chapters.title: A wife for Isaac
chapters.summary: Abraham's servant travels to Mesopotamia and prays for a sign. Rebekah offers water to him and his camels, and she agrees to return and marry Isaac.

chapters.title: Jacob and Esau
chapters.summary: Abraham dies and is buried by Isaac and Ishmael. Rebekah gives birth to twins, Esau and Jacob, and Esau sells his birthright for a bowl of stew.

chapters.title: Isaac and the wells
chapters.summary: God renews the promise to Isaac during a famine. Isaac repeats his father's half-truth about his wife, then digs wells and makes peace with the Philistines.

chapters.title: Jacob takes the blessing
chapters.summary: With Rebekah's help, Jacob deceives his blind father Isaac and receives the blessing meant for Esau. Esau vows revenge, and Jacob must flee.

chapters.title: Jacob's ladder
chapters.summary: On his way to Haran, Jacob dreams of a stairway reaching to heaven, with angels going up and down. God repeats the promise to him, and Jacob names the place Bethel.

chapters.title: Jacob marries Leah and Rachel
chapters.summary: Jacob works seven years for Rachel, but Laban tricks him into marrying Leah first. Jacob works another seven years for Rachel, and Leah begins to bear sons.

chapters.title: Jacob's family grows
chapters.summary: Rivalry between Rachel and Leah leads to more children through them and their servants, and finally Rachel bears Joseph. Jacob's flocks grow under Laban.

chapters.title: Jacob leaves Laban
chapters.summary: God tells Jacob to return home. He leaves secretly, Laban pursues him, and the two make a covenant of peace at a heap of stones.

chapters.title: Jacob wrestles with God
chapters.summary: Afraid to meet Esau, Jacob prays and sends gifts ahead. At night he wrestles with a man until dawn and is renamed Israel.

chapters.title: Jacob meets Esau
chapters.summary: Esau runs to embrace Jacob, and the brothers are reconciled. Jacob settles near Shechem and builds an altar.

chapters.title: Dinah and Shechem
chapters.summary: Shechem violates Jacob's daughter Dinah. Her brothers Simeon and Levi take violent revenge on the city, which troubles Jacob.

chapters.title: Return to Bethel
chapters.summary: Jacob's household puts away foreign gods and returns to Bethel, where God confirms the name Israel. Rachel dies giving birth to Benjamin, and Isaac dies.

chapters.title: Esau's descendants
chapters.summary: A record of Esau's family and the chiefs and kings of Edom, the nation that came from him.

chapters.title: Joseph sold into slavery
chapters.summary: Jacob's favorite son Joseph dreams of his family bowing to him. His jealous brothers sell him to traders bound for Egypt and tell their father he is dead.

chapters.title: Judah and Tamar
chapters.summary: Judah fails to give his widowed daughter-in-law Tamar the justice she is owed. She disguises herself to secure it, and Judah admits she is more righteous than he.

chapters.title: Joseph in Potiphar's house
chapters.summary: The Lord is with Joseph as he serves Potiphar. He refuses the advances of Potiphar's wife, is falsely accused, and is thrown into prison, where God is still with him.

chapters.title: Dreams in prison
chapters.summary: Joseph interprets the dreams of Pharaoh's cupbearer and baker. Both come true, but the cupbearer forgets him.

chapters.title: Joseph rises to power
chapters.summary: Joseph interprets Pharaoh's dreams of seven good years and seven years of famine. Pharaoh puts him in charge of all Egypt to prepare.

chapters.title: The brothers come to Egypt
chapters.summary: Famine drives Joseph's brothers to Egypt to buy grain. Joseph recognizes them, tests them, and keeps Simeon until they bring Benjamin.

chapters.title: The second journey
chapters.summary: Jacob reluctantly lets Benjamin go. Joseph hosts his brothers at a feast and is so moved by seeing Benjamin that he leaves the room to weep.

chapters.title: The silver cup
chapters.summary: Joseph's cup is planted in Benjamin's sack. Judah offers himself as a slave in Benjamin's place to spare their father grief.

chapters.title: Joseph reveals himself
chapters.summary: Joseph tells his brothers who he is and forgives them, saying God sent him ahead to save lives. He invites the whole family to Egypt.

chapters.title: Jacob goes to Egypt
chapters.summary: God reassures Jacob in a vision, and the family of seventy goes down to Egypt. Jacob and Joseph are reunited in Goshen.

chapters.title: Joseph and the famine
chapters.summary: Jacob meets Pharaoh and the family settles in Goshen. Joseph manages Egypt through the famine, and the dying Jacob asks to be buried in Canaan.

chapters.title: Jacob blesses Joseph's sons
chapters.summary: Jacob adopts Ephraim and Manasseh as his own and crosses his hands to give the younger the greater blessing.

chapters.title: Jacob blesses his sons
chapters.summary: On his deathbed Jacob speaks a blessing or warning over each of his twelve sons, foretelling a lasting rule for Judah. Then he dies.

chapters.title: Joseph's last words
chapters.summary: Jacob is buried in Canaan. Joseph reassures his fearful brothers that God meant their evil for good, and before he dies he asks that his bones be carried to the promised land.
